Tessa / Lauren — technical details below (keeping answers short so we can pass to Elena):

1) Export formats / delivery:  
- Tenant-scoped exports supported via: a) encrypted S3 archive (AES-256) generated in-region, b) JSONL/CSV bundles, c) continuous syslog streaming to a customer collector (TLS).
- Exports can be filtered by tenant id, time-window, and event-type (access, admin-audit, model-inference).

2) Residency:  
- Hosted EU regions (Frankfurt & Amsterdam) store primary logs on EU-only storage. Backups for hosted EU are kept in EU regions only; we do not replicate hosted-log backups to outside EU unless a customer opts into a cross-region DR plan.

3) Deletion & evidence:  
- For hosted customers: we perform a 3-step procedure: 
  a) Generate tenant-scoped export (signed manifest, SHA256 checksums).
  b) Run deterministic purge across hot/warm storage and mark objects with a deletion tombstone in the index.
  c) Final cold-store overwrite/purge per retention SLA.
- Evidence: we provide an export bundle (if requested), plus a signed deletion report containing run ID, timestamps, object checksums, and the purge job's audit log entry IDs. We can also include the internal job run output (redacted) for compliance review.
- Legal holds: deletion windows will be paused if a verified legal hold exists; we surface this in the deletion report.

4) Export SLA / performance:  
- Typical tenant export generation completes within 24 hours for <10GB. For 10–100GB we target 48 hours. Very large exports (>100GB) may take up to 72 hours depending on queue/backfill; we provide progress updates via the Console and a signed manifest when ready.

5) Private / on-prem options:  
- For Private (VPC) and on-prem packages, all logging can be routed to customer-managed S3 buckets or local syslog endpoints; retention is then under customer control (we still surface our audit IDs but no data leaves the customer environment unless explicitly exported).

Example commands (internal):
- Start export: redwood export logs --tenant-id=medsys-eu --from=2026-01-01 --to=2026-12-31 --format=jsonl --dest=s3://redwood-exports/medsys-2026/ --encrypt-key=customer-kms
- Purge job: redwood logs purge --tenant-id=medsys-eu --run-id=purge-20270105-01 --confirm

I'll attach the export runbook snippets and the residency matrix you already included. Happy to join a short call with Elena if helpful.

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — quick written answers to your follow-ups:  
- Backups & vaults: for hosted EU customers we do not copy operational backups outside EU regions by default. Backups are subject to the same purge workflows; when a purge is executed we run the purge against primary + backup indexes and include backup purge entries in the deletion report. For additional assurance we can provide a customer-scoped backup inventory and the purge job IDs that touched those vaults.
- Replay into Console: for VPC/private deployments we provide a rehydration utility (dry-run + replay) that can ingest exported JSONL bundles back into a customer-only analysis workspace (requires signed off SOP and access agreement). We do not accept rehydration into shared hosted stacks unless explicitly contracted.
- Signed manifests: yes — we can sign manifests with our org certificate (X.509) and include the signature in the bundle. That provides non-repudiation for the exported archive.
- Export SLA: confirm hosted EU default: <10GB = 24h, 10–100GB = 48h, >100GB = up to 72h (queue-dependent). We will include a clause in the SOW for expedited exports for a fee or as part of an enterprise SLA.
